text.p: Ameritech Corp and AT&T Corp said Monday they reached an agreement to resolve various disputes between them and to work toward bringing more competition and greater choice to consumers of all telecommunications services.

Terms of the setlements are confidential. One dispute resolved involves a lawsuit filed by Ameritech on December 19, 1996 concerning statements to industry analysts about Ameritech's operational support system interfaces for processing orders.

Although the two companies have their differences in connection with the issues to be addressed by Ameritech's filings for long distance authority under the new Telecommunications Act, they have agreed to work cooperatively to solve any issues that arise in connection with AT&T's use of Ameritech's operational support systems.
Another dispute the companies resolved concerned a series of lawsuits involving claims under a Mutual Credit Card Honoring Agreement.

The final dispute Ameritech and AT&T have resolved involves a proceeding before the Michigan Public Service Commission concerning provisioning and restoration of access facilities Ameritech provides to AT&T. The parties have agreed to a set of standards for the provisioning of access facilities and the restoration of facilities in the event of service interruption.
